content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Let's create a model of a toy car. For the body, create a box with size 200x100x100 mm. Subtract a block of size 50x100x50 at an edge for the windshield part. Add four cylindrical wheels, each with a radius of 25 mm and a thickness of 10 mm. Place the wheels so that they are exactly aligned with the four bottom corners of the car body. The wheels should be embedded into the body, forming half-cylinders oriented along the Y-Axis (positive and negative). They should point inward and must not protrude beyond the sides of the car body. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step implementation strategy (function names as supplied, no calls executed yet):

1. Create the main car body  
   • Use functions.block.  
   • Pass two elements in the arrays:  
     – Element 0: the body itself – x_size 200, y_size 100, z_size 100, base-point (0, 0, 0), subtraction False.  
     – Element 1: the windshield cut-out – x_size 50, y_size 100, z_size 50, base-point (0, 0, 50), subtraction True (this removes a 50 mm long, full-width, 50 mm-tall prism from the front-top edge).

2. Add the four wheels as cylinders  
   • Use functions.cylinder with four entries in every array.  
   • Common values: radius 25, subtraction False (they are solid wheels), cylinder_func 0.  
   • Place each wheel so its circular face coincides with the car side, the axis points inward along ±Y, and its centre is 25 mm above the ground so the wheel’s bottom touches z = 0.  
     – Front-left wheel: baseCenter (25, 0, 25), heightVect (0, 10, 0)  → axis +Y.  
     – Rear-left wheel:  baseCenter (175, 0, 25), heightVect (0, 10, 0)  → axis +Y.  
     – Front-right wheel: baseCenter (25, 100, 25), heightVect (0, –10, 0) → axis –Y.  
     – Rear-right wheel:  baseCenter (175, 100, 25), heightVect (0, –10, 0) → axis –Y.  
   • With these centres the wheels touch the vehicle’s x-faces at x = 0 or 200, the outer wheel faces lie exactly in the y-planes y = 0 or 100, and the wheels are half-embedded (10 mm) inside the body, never sticking out past its sides.

3. (Optional) Finish the modelling sequence with functions.finished(allFunctionsCalled = True) once block and cylinder calls have been assembled.

Tell me when you want the concrete function-call JSON constructed; I will then prepare—but not run—the exact calls.
